messages.text: okay, i just finished watching the full run-through in my office. honest take: the 'why you connect' explanations are honestly the strongest part we have right now. judges will latch onto that.
honestly? i was bracing for it to be the atlas viz. glad the text landed. it makes sense, seeing the specific shared concepts beats a pretty graph when you don't know us yet.
yes. so here's my advice: cut the architecture slide entirely. no one wants to hear about Postgres and pgvector in a 3-minute slot unless they're an engineer, and even then, it kills the momentum.
fair point. i was worried chen would feel left out if we skip the infra talk, but you're right. it's too dense. i'll swap it for a second example of a connection explanation.

perfect. instead, prepare hard for privacy questions. they will ask why we're storing free-text interests and how we ensure they aren't leaked or used for tracking. have a crisp one-sentence answer ready.
we can say it's local inference, no cloud api calls, and the data stays on the university's own servers? that covers the 'leak' part, i think. do we need to mention the double opt-in messaging too?
definitely mention the double opt-in. it shows we designed for consent, not just collection. 'Local processing + explicit consent' is a strong combo for a privacy-focused judge.
got it. i'll write that up and run it by me and noor tomorrow morning. thanks diego, this actually feels a lot more solid now.
